settlements.topic: The VERIFY registry: named checks, pure functions, observable evidence only (point 2, spec FN-11)
settlements.decision: A registry of 14 named checks, one pure Python function each: the twelve names of FN-11 (charter-stamp, workable, audience-split, atom-rules, judge-gate, price-kept, within-budget, order-registered, finding-per-item, pass-needs-proof, code-measure-wins, answer-recorded) plus the two floors of S2-models-06 (reply-valid, turn-posted). Each is fn(ev: Evidence, args) -> Outcome(ok, evidence<=2000, changed, na, waived). Evidence is built by the layer from hook data only: the node's replies (CallInfo.reply), the chat messages posted in the turn with their meta (message_posted), the latest data of goal.json, workflows.json, audits.json, realization.json and conflicts.json as saved this turn (record_saved) or read at turn start, the TurnInfo and the TurnOutcome, plus owners (atom id -> owner node, from the layer's own opens and J2's builder ids). No change to j2.py, no new hook. Phases: reply (judged on each reply, a failure is a live try), turn (judged once at turn end), event (answer-recorded). Kinds: gate (J2 retries) and override (J2's code corrects and the check proves the outcome). For each name the inputs, pass rule, evidence text, function turn and J2 stage, attempt budget and J2's recovery are in docs/design/function-nodes.md section 4; J2's recovery stays the default and the plugin's cap of 3 close runs is the ceiling. Recovery closes the atom with 'RECOVERED:' (repair, template, drop) or 'WAIVED:' (J2 accepts a concern) at the start of the last evidence; an unrecovered failure is verify_failed (S4-fnodes-08). FN-10 (the Audit independence backstop) is a clause of finding-per-item: a result row that names an atom owned by this department's Audit fails; J2's rows carry no atom today, so it never fires. FN-12: the judge's and planner's calls are charged to the Adaptation atom, and judge-gate only reads realization.json, so it needs no time budget. Where a thing is not observable the check reads J2's own posted note instead (atom-rules reads the 'Validator rejected' posts, price-kept the two Priority notes, the charter acceptance note) and a golden pins those strings. All five VERIFY lines of the cards are true as drawn, so no card text changes. The registry lives in the engine (new WP E8: registry.py, evidence.py); the library only lists the names in CheckTemplate. Supersedes S2-models-06: 'Version 1 check set: reply-valid and turn-posted', 'Not in v1: J2's named code checks as atom checks', the REJECTED clause 'J2's named code checks as atom checks in v1', and the generic template's single check turn-posted.
settlements.why: The cards promise five verify lines; with only two generic checks they would be words. Every J2 check the cards name is decidable from what the hooks already see, so the teeth can be real without touching j2.py. Pure functions with recorded fixtures are testable offline and mutation-testable, which the generic pair was not.
settlements.rejected: Only reply-valid and turn-posted (the cards would overstate); re-implementing J2's stateful _atom_problems purely (it needs the run's state, the output kind and the built page); parsing prompts for numbers where a posted meta or ledger input exists; a new _event hook in j2.py (outside the P8 budget); a shell runner with the plugin's 30 s alarm (pure checks need no subprocess).

settlements.topic: Atom grain: one atom per function turn, with llm, bash and manual work (point 3, FN-2 against S2-models-06)
settlements.decision: One work atom per function turn, from turn_started to turn_finished of the five function names. J2's re-asks inside the turn are tries (attempt) of the same atom; planner, judge, summariser, reviewer and template-spec calls are charged to the open atom and are not atoms. The work kind is llm when the turn calls a model, bash when it does not (Priority's envelope check within limits, Coordination's queue-empty hand-off to Audit, the charter-change Relay) and manual for the owner's question: a turn that ends paused is followed by one manual atom of the same node (always Identity's) whose check answer-recorded runs when the owner's message arrives. The declared kind is the template's prediction, from a file or the template and never from a reply: envelope is bash; schedule is bash iff workflows.json at turn start holds no registered or held workflow. Seen.work corrects a wrong guess at the first transition after the work (the stored work.dispatch_kind is replaced and notes gets 'declared bash, did llm'). Builders, the code validator and the confidence judge open no function atom. Words: the strip caption '1 step = 1 atom' becomes '1 turn = 1 atom' ('step' means a J2 loop step or a graph step node elsewhere); the label 'every AI step = one atom' becomes 'every call has an atom id'; the ledger line 'one record per atom attempt' becomes 'one row per call, by atom'; the router line 'cost per atom: usd and tokens' stays true (the sum over the atom's calls). Supersedes S2-models-06: the sentence 'a turn without any agent_turn call is closed once with the check turn-posted' (that turn is a bash atom, its check is still turn-posted) and the absence of any question atom; FN-2's 'an llm atom is one router call' (an atom has one or more calls).
settlements.why: J2's unit of work is the turn: the cards' WORK ATOM YIELDS lines (a charter, a verdict, a schedule, a finding) are one turn's yield, the engine hooks and ORCH-D10 say 'atom per turn', and re-asks map onto the plugin's attempts without changing J2. The strip promises 'AI call, code step, or a question to you', so bash and manual atoms must exist, but a question is not a model call and a code step is not a turn of its own.
settlements.rejected: One atom per router call (planner and judge calls are not steps; the strip's 'a TASK runs as atoms' would explode into hundreds); keeping code-only actions outside the atom loop (the floor and the graph counts would miss them); predicting the kind from the model reply; opening atoms lazily at the first call (it would break 'declared before the work').

settlements.topic: Mode: what 'hard' means when J2 already enforces replies and routes (point 4, FN-9 against S2-models-06)
settlements.decision: Version 1 observes and J2 stays byte-identical. 'Hard' is made precise in four parts. (1) An atom closes only through passing checks: the library's close_atom is the only place state becomes closed, and no flag or caller can skip a card or a ledger row. (2) Replies and routes are enforced by J2's own code today (re-ask once, repair, drop, template, _pick) and that stays the default; the closed reply models (reply-valid) and HANDOFFS (turn-posted) are the oracle the registry judges the outcome by, so a violation can no longer pass unseen but J2's behaviour is not changed. (3) The write-scope floor is warn-and-log: at message_posted a message by a function with no open atom, and at record_saved a record outside FunctionSpec.writes, writes one trace.jsonl line 'layer.touches_miss' and blocks nothing; it flips to hard only when the golden runs show none (a later decision). (4) SUTRA_NODES=on|off|enforce: on is the default, off selects EventHooks, enforce is reserved and the factory raises ValueError (S2-models-05 stands). Every hook body of the layer is wrapped: an error becomes a 'layer.error' trace line and never reaches J2 (no fatal flag is ever set). Changes to J2 behaviour: none listed; system_addendum stays empty, so the prompt goldens are byte-identical. Clarifies S2-models-05/06 (observe only) and FN-9; changes S2-models-06 only in that FunctionSpec.writes is 'recorded and warn-logged, not enforced' instead of 'recorded, not enforced'.
settlements.why: J2's code already re-asks, repairs and re-routes; making the layer block or retry would change D4's 'behaviour the owner sees in J2 stays' and the prompt goldens. A check that decides the atom's fate, never the turn's, is hard enough to make a violation visible and permanent in the Atom log, which is what the owner asked for ('verify is the teeth').
settlements.rejected: Blocking or re-asking a turn when a check fails in v1 (changes J2's recovery); hard write scope from day one (it would block legitimate J2 moves such as Priority re-pricing a ruling with J2_FIXES=1); a j2.py patch beyond P8; an enforce mode that is half built.

settlements.topic: Refuse: stored and carded, or nothing written (point 5, FN-3/FN-16 against S2-models-10)
settlements.decision: A refused open is stored (state refused, attempt 0), ledgered (Atom log status refused, reason = the refusal message) and carded (one line, ATOM REFUSED) in the node's own session, as S2-models-10 and library DL6 say. The v1 turn goes on without an atom (observe mode, S1-contracts-10). Production templates never refuse (tests prove every template opens), so a refusal means a template or registry bug made visible. The strip's refuse cell is rewritten to be true: title 'exit: refuse' (unchanged), line 1 'bad goal or check:' (unchanged), line 2 'logged as refused' (was 'nothing is written'; 17 characters, inside the cell width the old 18-character line used). Abandon keeps its cell ('reason required;' / 'no check, log row'). Supersedes FN-3 and FN-16 where they say 'nothing is written' (the plugin's silent stderr refusal).
settlements.why: The owner named four verbs with cards and a ledger row; a hidden refusal would make a missing atom look like a bug (S2-models-10). Storing it is also less code than special-casing a non-write, because the library already returns a stored refused atom with a Card.
settlements.rejected: The plugin's behaviour (a stderr line, no row, no card), which FN-16 itself calls a promise the code does not keep; hiding refused atoms as abandoned (S3-web-13(d), superseded by S4-fnodes-08).

settlements.topic: Chat sessions of function nodes and divisions; what a division click shows (point 6, FN-6/FN-7 against S2-models-11)
settlements.decision: One session per graph node stays (S2-models-11, draw.io steps 5 and 7), with these kinds: cs_org (the root, writable by the owner), department (writable, Identity's voice), division (a lens), function (read-only working log, five per department), step (read-only). Function nodes exist per department only; a division has none. A division's session keeps no conversation of its own, only notes ('Merged into X', 'Took in Y'): its transcript is the department session filtered to the tasks scoped to the division, plus those notes (ORCH-D1's filtered view), and a line written there is delivered to the department's Identity with scope_node_id (ORCH 5.5): one conversation, one writable voice. Identity's chat for the owner is the department session: the Identity chip and the department node open it (S3-web-05); Identity's own function session is its read-only working log and holds its atom cards, which the drawer lists from the atoms table. Only Identity ever receives the owner's words. Departments never move, merge or split (DL5), so no function node changes owner; a division merge or split touches no function node. What the UI shows on a division click: the node panel on the Chat tab with the lens header '<Division> is part of <Department>. This is <Department>'s Identity, showing the work for <Division>' and the link 'Show everything for <Department>' (opens the department session), the composer on; the Details tab shows 'Functions of <Department>' with five chips that open the department's function panels, and no goal, task or atoms. Supersedes the FN-6 sentence 'opens its department's Identity chat (a lens, not a second session)' in wording only: it is a lens with a session row; it does not change S2-models-11.
settlements.why: The published Chat sessions box says 'one per node' and draw.io step 7 names the division; a lens row keeps every node linked and keeps merge, split and move working (notes, filed_under) without a special case. The meaning of FN-6 (no second conversation, only Identity hears you) holds.
settlements.rejected: No session row for a division (FN-6 read literally: 'one per node' on the figure would be false, merge notes would have nowhere to live and carry_links would need a division exception); a separate writable conversation per division (two voices); opening the Identity working-log session on the Identity chip (rejected in S3-web-05).

settlements.topic: Cost and ledger: one atom id on every call, overhead keys, column names (point 7, FN-13 against S1-contracts-05/07/10 and S2-models-07)
settlements.decision: One rule: every model call is charged to exactly one atom id, written in usage_ledger.atom_id (TEXT, S1-contracts-05; index usage_atom(atom_id); no foreign key). (1) A call made inside an open function turn, helper calls (planner, judge, summariser, reviewer, template spec) included, carries that atom's id through llm.bind_atom. (2) A builder call carries J2's own tag.atom; the Projector stores it as '<run_id>:W-n.aK' (S2-models-10); an explicit tag wins over the binding. (3) Every other call carries an overhead key: the run's, for engine calls outside a turn (end-of-run review, template spec between turns), and the request's, for the chat agent. overhead_atom_id(owner_ref) = function_atom_id(atom_sid(owner_ref, 'overhead'), 1) in library types.py, owner_ref = the run id or 'req-<id>'; it matches the AtomId pattern, is not a third id scheme and has no atoms row (an accounting key, not a work atom: no goal, check, card or log row). The Router builds UsageIn.atom_id from tag.atom; the engine host binds the run overhead key at run_started and the layer rebinds it (not None) after every turn; AsyncConnector maps context.atom_id to CallTag.atom and the TurnRunner sets it to the request key on every call of the request. Invariants (contract tests): no provider usage row has atom_id NULL (stub rows carry it too); the per-atom sums equal the ledger total; the total with provider 'stub' excluded is the provider bill. AtomOut.usage sums usage_ledger by atom_id (S2-models-07). GET /api/usage/summary gains by=atom. Supersedes S1-contracts-10: 'clears it with llm.bind_atom(None) at turn_finished and on every run end path' (rebinds the run overhead key; None only in tests); S1-contracts-07: the context mapping list gains atom_id; S1-contracts-05: atom_id 'TEXT' nullable becomes 'never NULL for a row written by the engine host or the chat agent' (the connector layer still accepts an untagged call from other callers and stores NULL).
settlements.why: FN-13 asks that the ledger sum to the provider bill and that every call be attributable; the engine and the chat agent are the only two callers, so a default binding and one context key close the gap with no router change. Overhead keys reuse the function-atom id form, so S2-models-10's 'no third scheme' holds.

settlements.topic: Statuses: the final spec's four against the library's four, and the one mapping every surface uses (point 8, FN-18)
settlements.decision: Stored states stay the library's (open, closed, refused, abandoned). One pure library function atom_display_state(atom) gives the five display words (open, verify_failed, closed, refused, abandoned) that the card, the Atom log, the chip counts and AtomOut.state all use; the mapping table is docs/design/function-nodes.md section 6.2. verify_failed is derived, not stored: an atom the layer ends because its checks failed is stored abandoned with the new field Atom.abandon_code = 'verify_failed' (other codes: run_ended, replaced, manual; abandon_atom(atom, reason, now, *, code='manual', seen=None)). The layer makes that end at turn end, or at once on the third failing reply, after the final failing close_atom, so the cards are VERIFY FAILED then WORK ATOM ABANDONED and the atom rests as verify_failed. A failed try with tries left leaves the atom open (display open, pill 'in progress, attempt n'); a try that J2 then retried successfully ends closed 'on attempt n'. The word refused is a wire word (AtomOut.state has all five); atom/1 rows keep J2's four words, which are the same display words. LedgerRow.status becomes closed, verify_failed, abandoned or refused with the rule: closed => verify exit 0; verify_failed => verify {template, last failing exit_code} and a reason; abandoned and refused => a reason, no verify. The orchestrator stores the display word in atoms.display (computed by AtomStore.upsert from the Checked body, never from the event) with a CHECK and the index atoms_node_display(node_id, display). Supersedes: S2-models-06 and S2-models-07 (the rule 'verify_failed iff state is open, attempt is 3 and the last result of some check is non-zero' and the sentence 'After the third failed attempt the atom stays open; atom_display_state reports verify_failed'); library DL6 and section 7 ('verify_failed is an outcome, never a stored state' stays true as 'never a stored state'); S3-web-13(d) ('refused never leaves the API').
settlements.why: J2's retries are mostly one or two, not three, so a state defined at attempt 3 would never show; the failure that counts is 'tries used up and no recovery', which the layer knows at the turn end. Keeping the stored states the plugin's (ADR-038) and deriving the fifth word gives the spec's four statuses on every surface without a stored fifth state or a second SQL vocabulary for the same table.
settlements.rejected: A stored verify_failed state for function atoms (against ADR-038 and library DL6, and a second per-schema CHECK); leaving the atom open at attempt 3 (it would block the node's next atom); hiding refused as abandoned (S3-web-13(d): a missing atom would look like a bug); computing the display word in the UI (three surfaces would drift).

settlements.topic: The Atom log box against the atom_ledger table; verify_failed rows too (point 9, FN-19)
settlements.decision: The Atom log box of the figure is the atom_ledger table: append-only (triggers abort UPDATE and DELETE), one row per atom (UNIQUE atom_id), columns seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, atom_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, node_id TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('closed','verify_failed','abandoned','refused')) = the display word at the end of the atom (S4-fnodes-08), body TEXT NOT NULL = the library LedgerRow JSON, ts INTEGER NOT NULL. It is written only by AtomStore.append_ledger inside the Projector transaction, never by a node. A function atom brings its LedgerRow in the atom event at its terminal transition (field ledger, S2-models-07). For a builder atom (atom/1) the Projector builds the row with the library function ledger_row_from_view(view, node_id, department_id) the first time a view is terminal (closed, verify_failed or abandoned), so 'one row per atom' is true for builders too; the unique index makes a replay harmless. Per-try results stay on the atom (body.verify.checks[].results[], the 'what changed' lives in the evidence text), cost stays in usage_ledger by atom_id. New read route GET /api/atoms/log?node_id=&after=&limit= returns rows in seq order. Supersedes S2-models-07: 'append atom_ledger when ledger is present' (function atoms only) and the column list of ORCH 4.1 (seq, atom_id, status, body, ts); the unique index of S2-models-07 stays.
settlements.why: FN-19 wants a slim append-only box with verify_failed rows beside the strip; the table already exists and only needed its terminal words, a node column for per-node reads and builders. One row per atom needs the builder rows, which only the Projector can write (the engine's publisher emits J2 views).
settlements.rejected: A second table for the Atom log (two copies of one fact); a node writing its own log row (FN-17: the runtime writes it); logging only function atoms (the figure says one row per atom); a row for every failed try (tries live on the atom).

Drawn: line 1 persona, line 2 '<Function> · <open> open · <closed> closed', J2's status outline (neutral colour), tooltip '12 calls · 41 s · 9,120 tokens · 1 failed'. stats = {calls, seconds, tokens_in, tokens_out} from the node event plus {atoms_open, atoms_closed, atoms_failed, atoms_total} counted over atoms.display (failed = verify_failed). Drawer (NodeDetail: node, session, atoms, usage_total, task, archived_chats): node.meta is exactly goal, task, context, constraints, wait_on, hands_to, stats. Order: head (persona and function, status chip, node.detail, usage line from usage_total, counts from stats); Goal = meta.goal; Task = meta.task, 'Working for: <title> (<status>)' from NodeDetail.task, 'Waiting on you|<persona>' from meta.wait_on; Context 'What this function is given' = meta.context; Work atoms (n = stats.atoms_total; the open atom first, then the 20 newest; 'Show all' = GET /api/atoms?node_id=&limit=100&offset=) under the strip's legend 'open > work > verify, close; exits: refuse, abandon'; Constraints = meta.constraints; Hands to = meta.hands_to; the J2 block and 'Go to the <function> tab' (department page only). settlements.topic: Tests: what proves the function nodes (point 11)
settlements.decision: Six layers, each mapped to a work package (full list in docs/design/function-nodes.md section 9). Registry (E8): per check at least one pass, one fail and the na, override, recovered and waived cases as fixtures tests/engine/fixtures/fn_registry/<check>/<case>.json {evidence, expect}; purity (same result on a deep copy; open, time and sockets forbidden); parity with J2's own _stamp_check, workable, the audience regexes, design_problems and THRESHOLD. Mutation (E8): every check is replaced by always-ok and by always-fail and its cases must fail both ways; outcome mutants must flip their check (GRANT over budget posted as GRANT, a schedule with an unregistered id, a PASS row with an empty note, a rubric item measured but passed, a charter that fails the stamp). Layer (E6): hook sequences against fake J2 events (open, fail, close; refused; waived; recovered; abandon at run end; manual atom; overhead binding; errors swallowed; touches_miss only logs). Golden (E7): the mock Brew Lab through the stub connector with the layer on and with SUTRA_NODES=off gives identical [function, sha(system), sha(prompt)] lists; per function at least one atom of each kind it handles (Identity intake, audit and the manual atom; Adaptation propose; Priority price and envelope; Coordination schedule; Audit audit); one atom per turn; none open at run.ended; every atom has a check; ledger rows equal terminal atoms; no usage line without atom. Server (ORCH-6/ORCH-3): replay of the golden events gives atoms, display, atom_ledger (once per atom, append-only, atom/1 rows), cards, open_atom, atom_count and stats, and a second replay changes nothing; the org chat has no model prose. UI (UI-6): the drawer parse (fnode_view.test.js on the NodeDetail fixture), the whoLabel table (chat_view.test.js) and the browser test (Identity chip composer, four read-only chips, the division lens panel). Contract (CT-1): atom_id never NULL, node meta keys, and gen.py holding the strings of function-nodes.md section 12 (skipped with a printed reason until the diagram is patched).
settlements.why: The owner's headline requirement is that the nodes have teeth; a check nobody can fail is decoration, so every check is tested from both sides and by mutation. The golden run proves the whole path without a model, and the prompt equality proves J2 did not change.
settlements.rejected: Only a golden run (it passes with always-ok checks); live-model tests in the default suite (D8); testing the checks through a full J2 run only (slow and indirect).

settlements.topic: Who speaks to the owner: org chat, department chat, needs-you cards, and the 'who' labels (point 12, FN-8 against ORCH-D1)
settlements.decision: One rule: the owner reads prose from one kind of author, an Identity, verbatim. Everything else the owner sees is a record written by code and labelled 'Sutra': cards, template lines, errors, the status report. The chat agent's model output is structure only (ChatDecision, the chart change, the assignments); none of its sentences is shown. Org-level messages with no department (status, smalltalk, clarify, no fit) are answered by code; there is no root Identity because the root is not a department (library DL5 gives function nodes to departments only). Consequences: org chat cs_org shows the owner's lines, per request one code template line (add 'I set up a {name} team and gave it your request.', reuse, move, merge, split, none, plus smalltalk 'Tell me what you need and I will give it to the right team.'), the cards (chart_change, task, approval, choice, done, error) and the needs_you cards, which are the team's Identity question verbatim and are answered in the department session; clarify becomes the F3 choice card 'Which team fits best?' with up to 3 candidates and 'None of these'. The department chat holds the owner's lines and Identity's to_user lines (J2's Simple view), no cards. Labels (ChatView.whoLabel): user 'You'; sutra 'Sutra'; identity 'Client Lead (Identity)', prefixed '<department name> · ' in the org chat and on cards; adaptation 'Strategist (Adaptation)'; priority 'Prioritiser (Priority)'; coordination 'Scheduler (Coordination)'; audit 'Quality Reviewer (Audit)'; W-n 'W-n Builder'; validator 'Validator'; system 'System' (the last six show only in function logs and the Detailed view). Code changes: ChatDecision loses reply and clarify, AssignmentPlan loses reply, the violation code not_plain, plain_check and the plain-words regeneration go, T8 posts the code template, the prompts lose their reply sentences. settlements.topic: The source of the department goal now that node events carry none (point 13, S3-web-04 unresolved)
settlements.decision: There is no departments.goal: S2-models-14 already removed the column and the text 'an Identity goal also sets departments.goal'. The department's goal is its charter, <run folder>/goal.json (J2's file, family goal, validated by gate_record). Its readers are J2's own routes (the Goal tab, /api/state) and the function nodes' 'charter' context; no table copies it. The Projector reads no file and no event field for it. The closed charter-stamp atom of the Identity node (event atom, status closed, check charter-stamp) is the only signal that a charter exists or changed, and it is used for nothing but the graph.updated of the node. This closes S3-web-04's unresolved item and replaces its fallback ('leave departments.goal empty and fill it from goal.json when run.ended is projected') and S3-web unresolved item 3: there is no field to fill and no test about step labels.
settlements.why: The charter is per run and changes with every intake; a copy in SQLite would be a second source that goes stale, and nothing in the UI or the chat agent reads it (the chart's purpose is the chart's own). The final spec says the charter is the reference every node reads, which is the file.
settlements.rejected: A departments.goal column filled at run.ended (stale between runs, one more writer); a new event or event field for the goal (the event set is closed, S1-contracts-09); reading goal.json in the Projector on every Identity node event (file I/O in the one SQLite writer for no reader).

settlements.topic: The FunctionNode shape against the final spec: one field list for the DB body, the wire and the drawer (point 14)
settlements.decision: FunctionNode (body of graph_nodes) has the Node base (id '<dept>.<kind>', label = the function name, department_id, state in idle/running/waiting/waiting_on_you/fault, detail S(0,300), version, chat_session_id, edge_ids, ts_created, ts_updated) plus: kind; goal S(1,600) = FunctionSpec.goal (the J2 role sentence, standing); task S(1,200) = FunctionSpec.role (the J2 ROLE line such as 'J2.c prices, checks run limits', a string, no Task class); context [S(1,200)]<=40 = FunctionSpec.reads (names of the slice; Identity's has no money field); open_atom AtomId?; atom_count int>=0; wait_on null|'you'|function key|builder id; stats {calls, seconds, tokens{input, output}}; spec_version int>=1. goal, task, context and spec_version are written when the node is made (new_function_node) and by refresh_function_nodes(specs, nodes) at startup when FunctionSpec.version is higher; no event writes them. state, detail, wait_on and stats come from the node event; open_atom and atom_count from the atom events in the same transaction. Not stored: constraints (= FunctionSpec.may_not) and hands_to (= HANDOFFS[fn] as patched by S3-web-04) are read at request time, and stats.atoms_* are counted over atoms.display. last_seen does not exist (it is the node's detail). The spec's child extras (Identity blind_to and audiences, Adaptation memory and planning, Priority rate_card and bargain bounds, Coordination write_lock, Audit rubric) are not node fields: they are J2 behaviour held by j2.py and EngineSettings, and by FunctionSpec.reads and may_not, so the record is one shape for all five. The node event's optional task and context are trace-only and ignored by the Projector. The wire (S4-fnodes-10): meta {stats, wait_on} in GraphView; goal, task, context, constraints, wait_on, hands_to, stats in NodeDetail; stats.tokens_in/out = stats.tokens.input/output. The drawer reads exactly these keys. A test asserts meta.goal, task and context equal the stored body and constraints equal may_not. The spec's AgentNode.session_id map (provider -> id) is the connector's per-session provider id (S1-contracts-08); the node keeps one chat_session_id. Supersedes: S2-models-08 ('Node TASK = FunctionNode.task = Task{id, kind, summary, inputs, set_by, ts}', already replaced by S3-web-04), S1-contracts-09 ('the server derives last_seen from detail'), S3-web unresolved item 4.
settlements.why: It gives one list that the library, the table body, the wire and the drawer all use, drops the two fields no source defines (last_seen, a live Task) and keeps the three standing strings with the node so a node record is self-contained and testable, while the two derived lists cannot go stale.
settlements.rejected: A Task object on the node (the card shows the standing line; the live unit is the department's task and the atom's task_id); storing constraints and hands_to (they would duplicate FunctionSpec and HANDOFFS); building goal, task and context at read time only (the stored record would be incomplete); writing them from events (FN-4, FN-5).
